key_insight: MCDA dynamically refines brain-network augmentations and learns relationships across multiple graph views to improve rs-fMRI-based brain disorder classification, rather than cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The framework may support research into brain disorder classification and candidate functional-connectivity biomarkers, but clinical utility is not established.
method: Iteratively update graph topology using a Dynamic Augmentation Update module.
Combine self-aware and cross-sample augmentation to capture individual signatures and inter-subject differences.
Jointly optimize classification and topology-guided contrastive losses across original and augmented graphs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports outperforming state-of-the-art methods on two public rs-fMRI datasets totaling 1,236 subjects, without providing numerical performance estimates.
watch_item: Generalizability to independent clinical populations and robustness across imaging sites remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: MCDA: Multi-View Graph Contrastive Learning with Dynamic Topology Augmentation for Functional MRI Analysis
